_about: Newbury for tools/course/real/layout.py. Ring 0 = OSM's outer edge of the turf (point numbers on reference/newbury/plan-draft.png, lower panel). OSM's turf is about 55 m wide round the loop: the flat course outside and the jumps course inside, so the flat course's inside rail is taken 30 m in from the outer edge (offset 30). The spur at the far end (the round mile's chute) is narrow, so there the inside rail is its own west edge. Where the round course comes off the far bend it runs diagonally (north-west) into the straight course's inner side; the game's run-in is shared with the straight mile on the stands side, the round course's rail carrying on its diagonal into it. The 1m5f61y chute off the home bend is narrow: its inside rail starts 10 m in from its south edge.

stands._about: Newbury's stands, owner 18 Nov 19:38-19:39: 'same basic model' (as Doncaster) on his marked-up satellite view (1 the stand at the bend, angled; 2 the long stand, turned a little to look up the straight; 3 the stand beyond it, square on; 4 an area up the course on the stand side; 'festival' the infield opposite, along the inside rail from the bend up the course) and his old photo of Newbury's stands ('bit more pitched roof terrace etc': a brick block with a hipped roof, a long pitched-roof stand, and a separate roof-terrace stand with a little lookout pavilion on its roof). So: 1 the pitched-roof (gable) stand turned 45 to the run-in, 14 m off the turf; 2 the clock house (the brick block) and a second pitched-roof stand in one line turned 20, its left end on the front line; 3 low terraces and the roof-terrace stand with Rowley's little Victorian pavilion on its roof as the lookout. 4 is the stand-side festival zone (perimeter.festivals). Owner's mark-up on the plan, 19:42: 2 and 3 square on and set back (fronts about 65 m off the inside rail, as the real stands), in his boxes x -26..49 and 76..148; 4 the stand-side festival zone set back the same, x 170..377; 1 as it was.
